title: Current- and field-driven domain wall dynamics and chirality switching in a planar helimagnet
abstract: We study the effect of electric current and magnetic field on the dynamics of chirality in a helimagnet with a strong easy-plane anisotropy. Using a continuum theory, derived for a quasi-one-dimensional frustrated ferromagnet close to the Lifshitz point, we show that a domain wall connecting domains with opposite chiralities can be driven by the current via the dissipative (non-adiabatic) component of the spin-transfer torque. Further, it is demonstrated that the adiabatic part of the torque in the presence of a magnetic field breaks the symmetry of the effective magnetic potential energy with respect to the chirality. We show that the leading symmetry-breaking term arises in the third order in the magnetization gradient, and derive the conditions of the chirality switching. Our conclusions are supported by numerical spin-lattice simulations.
summary: The paper theoretically models how electric currents and magnetic fields drive domain wall dynamics and chirality switching in planar helimagnets. Using continuum theory, it shows that spin-transfer torques break chiral symmetry, enabling the manipulation of helical states. The findings provide quantitative predictions for pitch renormalization and domain wall velocities.
main_problem: The study investigates how electric current and external magnetic fields influence the dynamics of chirality switching in a planar helimagnet.
main_result: The combined action of field and current breaks chiral symmetry, allowing for domain wall motion driven by non-adiabatic spin-transfer torque. However, achieving chirality switching via nucleation is shown to be difficult or impossible under certain theoretical constraints.
method: The authors employ continuum theory derived near the Lifshitz point, analyzing an effective Lagrangian incorporating spin-transfer torques and external fields.
model_or_system: The system is a planar helimagnet with strong easy-plane anisotropy, modeled using a quasi-one-dimensional description parameterized by spherical angles. The dynamics are governed by an effective Lagrangian derived from the underlying Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Domain wall velocity (V_DW), renormalized helical pitch ($	ilde{q}$ or $\psi_R$), and the degree of out-of-plane magnetization ($\cos \vartheta$).
important_parameters: The ratio of anisotropy energy to exchange coupling ($K/J$), current density ($	ilde{v}$), and magnetic field strength ($	ilde{h}$).
main_assumptions: Approximations include neglecting higher-order gradient terms in the continuum theory, assuming $	ilde{	heta} \ll 1$, and analyzing the system near the Lifshitz point.
figures_summary: Figures compare theoretical predictions to spin-lattice simulations showing pitch renormalization ($	ilde{q}$ vs. $	ilde{v}$) and domain wall velocity scaling with system size ($N_x$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the continuum theory for the helimagnet, deriving the effective Lagrangian including torque terms, analyzing the effects of current (dissipative/adiabatic) on pitch renormalization, and finally investigating the conditions required for chirality switching via domain wall dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework connecting macroscopic transport phenomena (current/field) to microscopic magnetic order parameters (chirality), which is highly relevant for understanding spintronics in complex magnetic materials.
